column1: # The WW3 routines ported to Kokkos, one row each, read by scripts/port_score.py (`just port-score`).
# routine: the gprof name, module:routine in lower case (as kokkos/tools/profile names it)
# file: the WW3 file and lines, at the upstream commit in `ww3_rev`
# status: the furthest step passed, in this order:
#   ported   a Kokkos kernel exists in kokkos/src
#   L2       inside WW3 (the ww3-gpu/kokkos-st4 branch), the model's output agrees with the Fortran's
#   gpu      the same L2 replay passed on a CUDA backend
# evidence: the command or file that shows the status
# regtested: was the Kokkos code run inside WW3 and compared with the Fortran (the L2 replay,
#   `--ww3-gpu --cpu` pair to pair with `--ww3`)? "yes: <how>" or "no: <why>". The owner, 2026-10-14.
#   scripts/port_score.py --check refuses a row without it. The port has no tests of its own:
#   WW3's regtests are its only tests (docs/ADRs/ADR-0010-kokkos-validated-by-ww3-regtests-only.md).
# kokkos: the port's C++ files, comma-separated; kokkos/PORT_RANKING.md lists them per port.
# wired: does WW3 at the WW3/ pin call the Kokkos code, behind its run-time flag? "yes: <where>" or
#   "no: <why>". A row is "translated" when it exists, "ported" when wired is yes, "regtested" when
#   regtested is yes: the three levels of the website's numbers (scripts/port_score.py).
# ww3_rev / ww3_lines / ww3_routines / ww3_files: written by `scripts/port_score.py --measure` (needs WW3/);
# the time score uses docs/data/ww3_full_gprof.tsv (`just profile-case full`)
